title: Identity and associativity of the normalized module derived direct-image compositor
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be an admissible commutative condensed coefficient ring of [sk-def-localizing-closure]. For every scheme $T$ put $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T})$, where $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ is the pulled-back ring and the category is the ordinary unbounded module-object derived category [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Use the module direct images and inverse images of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], with the coefficient identifications induced by composition of pullbacks from the point and the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. For arbitrary scheme maps $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ\xrightarrow hW$, write $\kappa_{g,f}:R(gf)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg_*Rf_*$ for the comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], transported through [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. On a K-injective representative it is the inverse of the termwise module compositor of [def-sfb-module-lower-star-comp]. The two natural transformations satisfy
$$ (Rh_*\kappa_{g,f})\circ\kappa_{h,gf}=(\kappa_{h,g}Rf_*)\circ\kappa_{hg,f}. $$
The canonical comparison $R(1_T)_*\cong1_{D_T}$ is induced by the sectionwise identity direct image. With this comparison, both identity compositor constraints are identities. All equalities include canonical functor associators and the transport along equality of composite scheme maps. No properness, density, Noetherian hypothesis, or field of definition is required.

proof.text: For each scheme $T$ use its small site in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], write $B_T$ for the section-ring sheaf reconstructed from $\Lambda_T$, and write $E_T$ for the fixed internal/sectionwise equivalence. By [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport], $E_T$ is additive exact and identifies the module direct image with the sectionwise direct image for the structural ring map adjunct to $\alpha_f$. These are ringed-topos morphisms with commutative rings: the commutativity is part of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Their composition is the structural map for the composite scheme map. Indeed [lem-sfb-eta-comp] gives $\eta_{gf}=c_{g,f,\Lambda_X}\,g_*\eta_f\,\eta_g$. Apply [lem-sfb-section-ring-lax-pushforward-coherence] to base-change precomposition on these sites and these coefficient maps. Its composition and identity assertions identify the ordinary internal compositors with the sectionwise geometric compositors, including the coefficient actions. Thus this identification concerns the specified maps, and not just their endpoints.

proof.text: The adjunction $f^*\dashv f_*$ is supplied by [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], and its left adjoint is additive exact for every scheme morphism by [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main]. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] applies with $u=f_*$ and $v=f^*$: $f_*$ carries K-injective complexes to K-injective complexes. This applies also to $g,h$ and their composites. By [lem-pd-section-derived-pushpull-normalization], termwise $E_T$ induces an equivalence $\mathcal E_T=D(E_T)$, preserves and reflects K-injectives, and identifies the derived direct images together with their resolution transformations. Write its comparison as $a_f:\mathcal E_Y Rf_*\xrightarrow{\sim}R f_{*,\mathrm{sec}}\mathcal E_X$. All the hypotheses here concern arbitrary schemes and commutative condensed coefficients; no finite-type or field hypothesis has been introduced.

proof.text: Let $I$ be an internal K-injective complex on $X$. Step 2 says that $f_*I$ and $E_Y(f_*I)$ are K-injective. In the normalization of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] choose the identity resolution $j:E_Y(f_*I)\to E_Y(f_*I)$. Then the comparison, after identifying the composite ordinary direct image with the iterated one, is $[g_*j]=1$. Undoing that ordinary identification gives $[c_{g,f,I}^{-1}]:(gf)_*I\to g_*f_*I$, where $c_{g,f}$ is precisely [def-sfb-module-lower-star-comp] by Step 1. The comparisons $a_f$ of [lem-pd-section-derived-pushpull-normalization] respect the resolution transformations, so this is also the formula for the comparison transported to internal modules. It proves the normalization required in the item for every K-injective representative, with the inverse direction as stated.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-pur-ringed-derived-composition-cocycle] to the four ringed topoi $(T_{\mathrm{proet}},B_T)$ and the three morphisms of Step 1. Its $\kappa$ is the same normalized comparison as in Step 3. To spell out transport of the equation, let $A=a_{hgf}$ and let $B$ be the composite comparison from $\mathcal E_W Rh_*Rg_*Rf_*$ to $Rh_{*,\mathrm{sec}}Rg_{*,\mathrm{sec}}Rf_{*,\mathrm{sec}}\mathcal E_X$, obtained by successively using $a_h,a_g,a_f$. Put $L=(Rh_*\kappa_{g,f})\kappa_{h,gf}$ and $P=(\kappa_{h,g}Rf_*)\kappa_{hg,f}$. The resolution-compatible comparisons of [lem-pd-section-derived-pushpull-normalization] and the compositor identification of [lem-sfb-section-ring-lax-pushforward-coherence] give
$$\mathcal E_W L=B^{-1}(L_{\mathrm{sec}}\mathcal E_X)A,\qquad \mathcal E_W P=B^{-1}(P_{\mathrm{sec}}\mathcal E_X)A.$$
Here the intermediate $a_{gf}$ and $a_{hg}$ cancel against their inverses; naturality moves $a_h,a_g$ past the relevant components. This is the usual substitution of the transported comparison into each of the two composites. The cited ringed cocycle gives $L_{\mathrm{sec}}=P_{\mathrm{sec}}$. Since $\mathcal E_W$ is an equivalence and hence faithful on each morphism set, $L=P$ componentwise. Functor associators are inserted in the definition of $B$; equalities of composite scheme maps use the same geometric fibre-product identifications fixed in Step 1.

proof.text:
The identity comparison $\epsilon_T$ in [lem-pur-ringed-derived-composition-cocycle] is induced by the termwise identity direct image. Step 1 identifies this ordinary identity comparison with the sectionwise identity for internal modules, and [lem-pd-section-derived-pushpull-normalization] identifies their resolution transformations. Hence its transport is exactly the canonical $R(1_T)_*\cong1_{D_T}$ in the item. For example on a K-injective $I$ the identity resolution gives the identity of $I$ under the ordinary identity-direct-image identification. The two ringed equations in the cited cocycle theorem therefore transport, by the same cancellation of comparison isomorphisms as in Step 4, to
$$(\epsilon_Y Rf_*)\circ\kappa_{1_Y,f}=1_{Rf_*},\qquad (Rf_*\epsilon_X)\circ\kappa_{f,1_X}=1_{Rf_*}.$$
These are precisely both identity compositor constraints. The transported equations include the canonical unitors and equality identifications of scheme maps. The argument uses small-site derived categories and exact inverse image only; it places no properness, density, Noetherian or field condition on the maps.
